We covered what code coverage measures,
and how to calculate it with `pytest-cov`,
in [Testing: evaluating test suite quality](1050-testing-quality.qmd).
Here we measure the coverage of our package.

In a package, we add `pytest-cov` as a development dependency with Poetry:

```bash
poetry add --group dev pytest-cov
```

and run it through Poetry, for example `poetry run pytest --cov=src`.

## Using our toy package example

Let's go back to our previous packaging function and tests.
For reference, this was our function


```{python}
def count_char(input_string):
    if not isinstance(input_string, str):
        raise TypeError(f"Expected input to be str, got {type(input_string)}")
    len(input_string)
```

and the tests we wrote

```python
import pytest

from countchar.count_char import count_char


@pytest.fixture
def text_data():
    file_path = "tests/text.txt"
    with open(file_path, 'r') as file:
        lines = file.readlines()
    return lines


def test_line_1(text_data):
    string = text_data[0]
    assert count_char(string) == 34

def test_line_2(text_data):
    string = text_data[1]
    assert count_char(string) == 10

def test_line_3(text_data):
    string = text_data[2]
    assert count_char(string) == 8
```

We can now look at the line and branch coverage of our current package files


```bash
pytest tests/ --cov=countchar # line coverage
pytest --cov=countchar --cov-branch # branch coverage
```

and generate the document for a coverage report

```bash
pytest --cov=countchar --cov-report html
```

## Reporting coverage badges

<https://codecov.io/> is a service that can take our `pytest` information and
give us a visualization of our test coverage
and also give us a badge we can display in our repository.

More detail about creating and linking Codecov to our repository
is in this section of the textbook: <https://py-pkgs.org/08-ci-cd#recording-code-coverage>

General steps:

- log in to <https://codecov.io/> with your GitHub account
- install the Codecov GitHub app
  (if you're using a personal account, your organization may have it already installed)
    - make sure the application can see your repository in the app settings
- find the repo on Codecov
- click configure
- set up the Codecov action
    - use GitHub Actions
    - select pytest
    - change `--cov-report=xml`
        - `pytest --cov --cov-branch --cov-report=xml`
    - get token info for `CODECOV_TOKEN` (from the configure page)
    - when CI runs, you will see a URL to the coverage results
      in that particular step's output (else you probably didn't have a token)
    - refresh the Codecov repo page
- badge
    - on the configuration page, there's a badge + graphs section
    - copy the Markdown badge (we are using Quarto + quartodoc; rst is for Sphinx)
